description: The auth plumbing: extend the JWT payload/user types + the authenticate middleware (pre-tenant-context, privilegedPrisma, membership load + membershipStatus/institution ACTIVE + permissionsVersion freshness, fail-closed, SUPER_ADMIN branch, request.auth + request.tenant), build the central authz engine (can / requirePermission pure-check / requireModuleActive permissive stub / canOnResource documented-only / shared resolvePermissions normalizer), and resolve roles/permissions at login to sign the canonical dual-shape token. Depends on FEAT-001 (PermissionKey, catalogue) and FEAT-002 (the membership/role/permission tables + generated client). Authoritative behaviour = design §6 and §12. No route is flipped yet (FEAT-004); the legacy guards keep working, so the app stays green.
steps: In c:/campusgate/apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts extend the `declare module '@fastify/jwt'` payload AND user with membershipId: string | null, roles: string[], permissions: string[], permissionsVersion: number | null (KEEP role, institutionId, jti). Add request.auth and request.tenant typing (augment FastifyRequest) with auth: { userId, membershipId, institutionId, roles, permissions, permissionsVersion } and tenant?: { institutionId }.

Extend `authenticate` per design §6.3 keeping EVERY existing check in place (jwtVerify; jti session exists && !revoked via privilegedPrisma; user accountStatus ACTIVE; institution.status ACTIVE). Then: if role !== 'SUPER_ADMIN', load the membership by (userId, institutionId) via privilegedPrisma selecting { id, membershipStatus, permissionsVersion, roles: { role: { key, permissions: { permission: { key } } } } }; membership missing → 401 (log warn with userId); membershipStatus SUSPENDED → 403 { error: 'Membership suspended' } (log info); DB error → 500 fail-closed, no request.auth; apply the permissionsVersion freshness compare (if token.permissionsVersion !== db.permissionsVersion, re-resolve permissions from the loaded rows via the shared resolvePermissions helper, fail-closed 500 on error); attach request.auth = { userId, membershipId, institutionId, roles, permissions, permissionsVersion } and request.tenant = { institutionId }. For SUPER_ADMIN: skip the membership load + version compare, set request.auth = { userId, membershipId: null, institutionId: <PLATFORM id, logging only>, roles: ['SUPER_ADMIN'], permissions: <platform keys>, permissionsVersion: null }, and LEAVE request.tenant undefined (never feed the PLATFORM id to app.current_institution_id). Keep request.user populated incl. legacy role/jti. Leave requireRole/requireTenantRole/requireSuperAdmin unchanged (they stay the shim for un-flipped routes).

Create c:/campusgate/apps/api/src/services/authz-engine.ts per design §6.4 (do NOT modify the existing authz.ts): `export function can(auth, permission: PermissionKey): boolean` returning auth.permissions.includes(permission); `export function requirePermission(permission: PermissionKey)` returning a Fastify preHandler that is a PURE can-check — it does NOT call authenticate; if request.auth is unset it logs at ERROR with the route path + permission key then replies 401 (defensive wiring-bug path), else if !can it logs at INFO then replies 403 { error: `Forbidden: missing permission ${permission}` }, else passes; `export function requireModuleActive(moduleKey: string)` returning a preHandler that always allows and carries the EXACT marker comment `// PHASE-0 STUB: permits all; real module-activation enforcement lands in the module-entitlement phase`; a commented-out documented-only canOnResource signature (not exported). Add `export function resolvePermissions(roles): string[]` that flattens roles[].role.permissions[].permission.key into [...new Set(keys)].sort() — this single helper is imported by BOTH login (FEAT-003 step 4) and the authenticate re-resolve path (step 2) so the sets are byte-identical.

In c:/campusgate/apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts /login, after the existing credential/account/institution checks: for a non-SUPER_ADMIN user load the membership (via privilegedPrisma) with its roles + permissions, compute roles/permissions via resolvePermissions and read permissionsVersion; for SUPER_ADMIN use roles=['SUPER_ADMIN'] + the platform permission keys, membershipId=null, permissionsVersion=null. Sign the canonical payload `{ userId, membershipId, institutionId, roles, permissions, permissionsVersion, role, jti }` (KEEP the legacy role claim). Leave the session-create, security-event, and response body behaviour otherwise unchanged.

Add unit tests (mocked @campusgate/db, no DB) under apps/api/src/services/__tests__/ and/or apps/api/src/middleware/__tests__/: can(); resolvePermissions dedup+sort and that login-path vs re-resolve-path yield byte-identical arrays for a multi-role input; ROLE_PERMISSIONS resolution (given roles → expected permission set); requirePermission returns 403 on missing and passes on present with a mocked request.auth, and returns 401 (not throw) when request.auth is unset; a requireModuleActive permit-all pin test; authenticate's SUPER_ADMIN branch vs membership branch; the permissionsVersion mismatch → re-resolve path.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build --workspace @campusgate/api` typechecks clean with the extended FastifyJWT types, authenticate, the new engine, and the login resolver
The /login signed token carries BOTH the new permissions array and the legacy role claim (asserted by a unit test)
requirePermission is a pure can-check that never calls authenticate; it 401s (not throws) when request.auth is unset and 403s on a missing permission
requireModuleActive permits every request and carries the verbatim PHASE-0 STUB marker comment; a unit test pins the permit-all behaviour
resolvePermissions produces a de-duplicated, sorted array and the login and re-resolve paths produce byte-identical sets (unit test)
The full apps/api unit suite passes and no route behaviour changes yet (legacy guards still own authorization until FEAT-004)
verification: From repo root: `npm run build --workspace @campusgate/api` succeeds
From apps/api: `npx vitest run` — the new engine/middleware/login unit tests pass and the pre-existing suite stays green
findings:
DONE. Auth plumbing complete; no route flipped (FEAT-004 owns that). Build typecheck green (`npm run build --workspace @campusgate/api`, exit 0). Full api suite green: 15 files / 130 tests, including the live cross-tenant escape suite. The legacy requireRole/requireTenantRole/requireSuperAdmin shim is UNCHANGED and still works (they call authenticate internally, which now also resolves the membership).

=== FILES CHANGED ===
- apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts: extended FastifyJWT payload+user to the canonical dual-shape { userId, membershipId: string|null, institutionId, roles: string[], permissions: string[], permissionsVersion: number|null, role (legacy UserRole), jti? }; augmented FastifyRequest with `auth?: RequestAuth` and `tenant?: { institutionId: string }`; exported `interface RequestAuth`; extended `authenticate`.
- apps/api/src/services/authz-engine.ts (NEW): resolvePermissions, can, requirePermission, requireModuleActive (+ documented-only canOnResource comment). Did NOT touch the existing authz.ts.
- apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts: /login now resolves membership (privilegedPrisma) + signs the canonical dual-shape token keeping the legacy `role` claim.
- Tests added: apps/api/src/services/__tests__/authz-engine.test.ts, apps/api/src/middleware/__tests__/authenticate.test.ts, apps/api/src/routes/__tests__/login-token-shape.test.ts.
- Pre-existing route tests updated (mock fixtures only, no behaviour change): added an `institutionMembership: { findUnique }` delegate returning an ACTIVE membership (roles:[]) to admin-config-calendar, analytics, emergency-alerts, gate-health, pass-revocation-summary, tenant-boundary integration tests — required because the legacy guards call authenticate, which now loads the membership via privilegedPrisma.institutionMembership.findUnique (delegate was previously unmocked -> threw -> 500 fail-closed). Empty roles are fine there: legacy guards read request.user.role, not permissions.

=== resolvePermissions SIGNATURE (FEAT-004 relies on this) ===
`export function resolvePermissions(roles: ResolvableMembershipRole[]): string[]` in apps/api/src/services/authz-engine.ts. `ResolvableMembershipRole = { role: { permissions: { permission: { key: string } }[] } }` (exported). It flattens roles[].role.permissions[].permission.key into `[...new Set(keys)].sort()`. This SAME helper is used by login (auth.ts) and the authenticate re-resolve path, so the token set and any re-resolved set are byte-identical. Unit-pinned: login-path vs re-resolve-path arrays are JSON-identical for a multi-role (ADMIN+HOD) input.

=== request.auth SHAPE (what FEAT-004 reads via requirePermission) ===
`request.auth?: RequestAuth` where `RequestAuth = { userId: string; membershipId: string | null; institutionId: string; roles: string[]; permissions: string[]; permissionsVersion: number | null }` (exported from apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts; import with `import type { RequestAuth } from "../middleware/auth.js"`). Tenant actor: membershipId set, permissions = resolved keys, request.tenant = { institutionId }. SUPER_ADMIN: membershipId null, permissionsVersion null, roles ['SUPER_ADMIN'], permissions = sorted platform.* keys, institutionId = PLATFORM id (logging only), and request.tenant LEFT UNDEFINED. `request.user` still carries the legacy `role`/`jti` plus the new fields.

=== ENGINE CONTRACT (for FEAT-004 route flips) ===
- `requirePermission(permission: PermissionKey)` -> Fastify preHandler, PURE can-check, NEVER calls authenticate. If request.auth unset -> logs ERROR (method+routeOptions.url+permission) then 401 { error: 'Unauthorized' } (defensive wiring-bug path, not a throw). If !can -> logs INFO then 403 { error: `Forbidden: missing permission ${permission}` }. Else passes. So FEAT-004 must install exactly ONE top-level bare `authenticate` hook per flipped file (replacing the requireTenantRole hook) + per-route requirePermission(key). A SUPER_ADMIN holds only platform.* keys so 403s on every tenant requirePermission (matches today's requireTenantRole rejection).
- `requireModuleActive(moduleKey)` -> preHandler PHASE-0 STUB, permits ALL (verbatim marker comment present), pinned by a permit-all unit test.
- `can(auth, permission)` -> auth.permissions.includes(permission).

=== authenticate PIPELINE (design §6.3) ===
Kept every existing check (jwtVerify; jti session exists && !revoked via privilegedPrisma; user accountStatus ACTIVE; institution.status ACTIVE). Then: SUPER_ADMIN -> skip membership load + version compare, set request.auth (membershipId null, permissionsVersion null, platform perms), request.tenant left undefined. Non-SUPER_ADMIN -> load membership via privilegedPrisma.institutionMembership.findUnique({ where: { userId_institutionId: { userId, institutionId } }, select: { id, membershipStatus, permissionsVersion, roles: { role: { key, permissions: { permission: { key } } } } } }); missing -> 401 (log warn + userId); SUSPENDED -> 403 { error: 'Membership suspended' } (log info); DB error -> 500 fail-closed, no request.auth (log error); permissionsVersion mismatch (token.version !== db.version) -> re-resolve via resolvePermissions (fail-closed 500 on error), else reuse token.permissions; attach request.auth + request.tenant; keep request.user with legacy role/jti. Compound-unique name is `userId_institutionId` (from @@unique([userId, institutionId])).
